name: geo-topic-agent
optional_tools: XMLRiver region files: https://xmlriver.com/files/geo.csv and https://xmlriver.com/files/langs.xlsx
DataForSEO credentials for approved Google Organic Live collection
Playwright for rendered screenshots and browser text extraction
XMLRiver/DataForSEO for approved live citation visibility tracking
known_limitations: Future live external collection remains approval-gated, credential-gated, and budget-gated; live proof must be recorded in the project quality gates for the approved topic and scope.
DataForSEO adapter currently supports Google Organic Live Advanced; other DataForSEO engines need new fixtures before enablement.
Base runtime produces lower-assurance SERP/AI analysis when no provider evidence or manual imports exist.
Semantic SEO TZ generation is invoked only through an explicitly approved command template; without generator access, the agent produces only the handoff JSON and report.
Full live-proven 100% claim requires every references/final-evidence-contract.json item to be external_pass; user-approved descopes create a limited ready_with_descopes claim, not live evidence.

Rendered screenshot and rendered DOM text evidence require Playwright in the target environment; without it, the LLM accessibility audit records blocked_missing_playwright and still reports robots, server, clean-content, and commercial extraction evidence.
QFO query-batch analysis requires explicit network and paid-provider approval for live XMLRiver SERP+AI collection; ChatGPT QFO import is optional and user-supplied.

XMLRiver live collection requires explicit search engine, region, language, requested top URL count (`--depth`, not pagination pages), calculated paid page request count, XMLRiver max thread scope (`XMLRIVER_MAX_THREADS=10`), and budget scope; Google loc IDs come from https://xmlriver.com/files/geo.csv, and Yandex uses numeric lr region id plus lang.
Page TZ generation is deterministic and local-first; competitor HTTP fetching is approval-gated and weak/blocked parses must be surfaced or replaced with local snapshots.
The required attribution notice and LICENSE.md must remain in runtime exports; removing or bypassing them violates the usage license.
Product placement opportunities are draft strategy ideas only; the agent must not claim that external placements were secured or publish outreach/content without separate approval.

Project context collection is a product/business discovery workflow and does not perform accessibility, robots, sitemap, user-agent, WAF, anti-bot, or LLM access audits; those are separate explicit commands.

After successful deep project-context collection, the next offered workflow is site-level audit plus target-page LLM accessibility audit; topic/semantic cluster intake comes after that audit is completed or declined.
Accessibility audit answers are checklist-first and HTTP bot probes must use full User-Agent strings; short bot tokens are only robots.txt tokens.

Antigravity and generic-agent adapters are thin native entrypoints over the canonical AGENTS.md router; if the host runtime has no native skill packaging, keep canonical skills/ plus mirrored .agents/.claude skill folders.

Generated reports, CSVs, JSON/JSONL summaries, and user-approved HTML analytics artifacts enforce UTF-8 artifact writing; raw provider/user evidence under data/raw and data/import is preserved separately and may require normalization before reporting.
XMLRiver provider/account errors are preserved as provider_error and do not count as negative visibility measurements.
The first QFO evidence pass does not produce an approved content plan; agent reasoning plus explicit user approval is required.
Installed commands use the persistent `.geo-topic-agent-runtime/geo_agent_cli.py` launcher; temporary PYTHONPATH setup is neither required nor supported as the normal path.

Full first-run path is environment adaptation -> deep site/product/brand context -> explicit confirmation of all brand variants -> site audit plus target-page LLM audit decisions -> topic plus user semantic cluster -> QFO/content plan -> page TZ -> monitoring.

Fast mode accepts a cluster for local planning, but live paid execution requires explicit engines, region/city, language, top-N URL depth, exact query inventory, calculated request scope, and approval bound to those values.
The runtime ships dashboard knowledge/data-contract guidance only; no dashboard UI, HTML/CSS/JS, frontend, mock data, fixed layout, client data, or test project is bundled.
